To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TRPV4 is involved in the autoregulatory response of the CBF to changes in fluid viscosity.
the TRPV4 channel participates in the coupling of the fluid viscosity changes to ciliary activity.

(1) The TRPV4 channel is a mechanosensitive channel that participates in the autoregulatory response of the CBF to changes in mucus viscosity; (2) TRPV4 channel activation leads to a Ca2+ signal in ciliated cells, which in turn, is required for the autonomic regulation of the CBF; (3) TRPV4 activation in ciliated cells is mediated by phospholipase-dependent mechanisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and cellular aspects of the coupling of viscous load to ciliary activity in ciliated cells.
the role of TRPV4 in epithelial ciliated cell autoregulation.
understanding the molecular mechanisms involved in the autoregulatory response of the CBF in ciliated cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TRPV4 channels are involved in the coupling between mechanical stimulation and the autoregulatory response of CBF.
TRPV4 is involved in the autoregulatory response of ciliary beat to viscous load.
TRPV4 channel is a key player in autoregulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TRPV4 is a candidate to participate as the mechano-sensor that couples the viscous load to the autoregulatory response of the CBF.
the TRPV4 channel is a mechanosensor that participates in the autoregulatory response to the viscous load in ciliated cells.
the TRPV4 channel is a candidate to be involved in the coupling between the viscous properties of the fluid and the ciliary beating.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TRPV4 channel is the first molecular component of the viscous load–sensing machinery that controls ciliary activity.
TRPV4 is a candidate to participate as a mechanotransducer that links changes in fluid viscosity to the autoregulatory response of the CBF in ciliated cells.
the TRPV4 channel is a key component in the coupling of mechanical stimuli to ciliary beating.
